item.title: U.S. Supreme Court rebuffs challenge to ban on gun ownership by nonviolent felons
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court refused to hear a case challenging the federal ban on gun ownership by nonviolent felons, upholding the Gun Control Act of 1968.

item.title: Applications sought for 10th District judgeships
item.description: Commission is accepting applications for three judge vacancies in the 10th District due to retirements. Deadline is March 23, with interviews in April.

item.title: Quandaries & Quagmires: Discipline prosecutors for good faith mistakes?
item.description: Legal scholar challenges proposals to discipline prosecutors for good-faith trial mistakes, citing Minnesota ethics rulings and Supreme Court precedent.

item.title: Kramer joins Uniform State Laws Commission
item.description: Liz Kramer, Minnesota’s solicitor general, was appointed to the Commission on Uniform State Laws to serve until May 31, 2027, replacing the late Melissa Hortman.

item.title: Justice Department ends fight over Trump’s law firm orders
item.description: The U.S. Justice Department dropped its appeal to revive Trump’s executive orders targeting law firms.

item.title: Conviction reversed over defendant competence doubt
item.description: Minnesota Court of Appeals reverses attempted aggravated robbery conviction, ruling district court erred in competency finding.

item.title: Moriarty’s office investigating top Border Patrol official, other agents
item.description: Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty is investigating federal Border Patrol agents, including Gregory Bovino, for potentially unlawful actions during a crackdown on undocumented immigrants.

item.title: Trump administration relaunches defense of law firm executive orders
item.description: The U.S. Justice Department reversed its decision and will continue to defend Trump-era executive orders targeting four law firms over legal work and affiliations.

item.title: Trade court braces for surge in tariff refund suits
item.description: Importers file 2,000 cases at the U.S. Court of International Trade seeking $130B in tariff refunds after the Supreme Court struck down Trump tariffs.

item.title: Court rejects takings claim over Floyd memorial barriers
item.description: Minnesota Court of Appeals rejects $30M unconstitutional takings lawsuit against Minneapolis over George Floyd memorial barriers and access claims.
